subject.title: Permanent Road Division No. 1000, Zone No. 9B (Harris Annex) — Measure Q (Harris Annex Permanent Road Division Special Tax)

text: Shall the County of San Diego, beginning Fiscal Year 2027-28 and annually thereafter, levy a special tax of up to $1,000 per developed / $375 per undeveloped parcel within Permanent Road Division No. 1000, Zone No. 9B – Harris Annex, replacing the existing assessment? The tax may be adjusted by up to 5% annually based on the Los Angeles Construction Cost Index or a comparable Southern California index and remain until modified or dissolved by law.
This measure requires 2/3rds Majority of those voting on the measure.

A “YES” vote is in favor of authorizing the County of San Diego to replace the existing assessment with a special tax of up to $1,000 per developed parcel and up to $375 per undeveloped parcel to fund ongoing road maintenance within the Permanent Road Division.

A “NO” vote is against authorizing the County of San Diego to replace the existing assessment with a special tax $1,000 per developed parcel and up to $375 per undeveloped parcel to fund ongoing road maintenance within the Permanent Road Division.

strong: PERMANENT ROAD DIVISION ZONE 9B HARRIS ANNEX SPECIAL

text: The Board of Supervisors for the County of San Diego placed this Measure on the ballot.

If this Measure is approved by two-thirds of the votes cast, parcels within Permanent Road Division Zone 9B Harris Annex shall pay a maximum parcel tax of $1,000 per parcel for each developed parcel and $375 per parcel for each undeveloped parcel commencing in Fiscal Year 2027-2028. The stated purpose of the special tax is to fund ongoing road maintenance, which includes administrative expenses. The special tax will continue to be collected in the Permanent Road Division until amended, repealed or suspended by the Board of Supervisors. The special tax will replace the existing assessment imposed in the Permanent Road Division by repealing Ordinance No. 9165. Total estimated revenue derived from the special tax from the 53 developed and 3 undeveloped parcels currently in the Permanent Road Division for the first fiscal year is $54,125. The special tax is subject to adjustment, not to exceed 5% per fiscal year, to account for any inflation as measured by the Los Angeles Construction Cost Index or a comparable Southern California construction cost index.
